english_weird.note: The English edition already has two collisions (E: Execution vs E1-E2 Windows track; D: Data vs section D), resolved by context: phases appear as 'W: Weird' headers and 'phase' wording, exercises as 'E1' or 'Exercise D'.

bicho.note: Plan N5 anticipated only B. The inventory also finds C (phase 3, Camino indirecto) colliding with C1-C3. Letters I, H, O are free. B and C are each reused heavily (B1-B22, C1-C3), so every phase reference must carry the word 'fase' or the phase name next to the letter and every exercise reference must carry its digit (or 'ejercicio D'). The phase lint (I14) must reject a bare letter in a phase context and a bare 'B'/'C' followed by a digit in a phase context.

torce.note: Runner-up alphabet: collides on two letters as well, same as English, so BICHO is no worse than TORCE on N5 (both have two collisions) and the plan's trigger 'choose TORCE if B collides badly' does not hold on the evidence.

collisions.recommendation: Keep BICHO as provisional default. Record in decisions-provisional.md that C also collides, and make the phase lint (I14) context-based as in plan 2.5.

frozen_conflicts.note: No frozen file (locked-code.sha256) contains a phase letter used as a phase. The Mermaid node IDs W E I R D live in docs/curriculum.md (Markdown, translatable) and stay unchanged by design.
